solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reduce in complexity provided that small hint is circulated

indicators.note: something circulated has a ring passed round it, so one piece sits inside the others here

blocks.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small
to hint is to suggest without saying outright
a conditional conjunction

explanation.surface: A dry note on simplifying things, as long as a small clue is passed around the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provided that' is the piece wrapped, not the wrapper, even though it comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To simplify something is to make it less complicated, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Rarely graft in European ranch when drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters lurch into a fresh order

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tipsy gardener attempts some grafting on a ranch in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' tells you the definition is a rare word: ENARCH is an old spelling of inarch, a grafting technique.
explanation.definitionFit: Inarching, or enarching, joins a growing plant to a stock while both remain rooted, a specialised horticultural graft.

clue.text: Pulled out permit to circumvent fine

indicators.note: to circumvent is to go round something, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: to let is to allow
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws a permit application to dodge paying a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has pulled out of an event has departed or quit it, the past tense of leave.

clue.text: Good way to enclose air on this?

definitions.text: Good way to enclose air on this?

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
ST, street, is a way
to ring something is to encircle it

explanation.surface: A musical question about where to play an air.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Bach's Air on the G String is played on the violin's lowest string.
explanation.definitionFit: Bach's famous orchestral Air is arranged to be played wholly on the violin's lowest string, tuned to G.

clue.text: Bird's fresh meat cut

blocks.note: green means new or unripe
shank is a cut of meat from the leg

explanation.surface: A butcher's note on a bird and some freshly cut meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The greenshank is a grey wading bird of the sandpiper family with long greenish legs.

clue.text: Wearing suit to a greater extent

blocks.note: first meaning: a card hand made up of the suit of spades
second meaning: an idiom for abundantly or much more so

explanation.surface: Someone dressing up in a suit even more than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing, but it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in large amounts or emphatically, and literally describes cards belonging to the spade suit.

clue.text: Spring in Guernsey's awful when sun about to disappear

indicators.note: something about to disappear is going away, so those letters are dropped from the rest
awful suggests something badly made, so the remaining letters get jumbled

blocks.note: the island name with its S included
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A grumble that Guernsey's weather turns dreadful once the sun goes in.
explanation.walkthrough: Take S, U and N out of GUERNSEYS to leave GEREYS, then rearrange. Guernsey is a Channel Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a hot spring that periodically shoots water and steam into the air.

clue.text: Jack by bar emptied expensive spirit

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece sits beside the next
an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only its first and last letters

blocks.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
an inn is a pub or bar
the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: Jack leaves the bar after an expensive spirit has been drained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like a drink to go with the bar; it is a supernatural being.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinnee, or genie, is a supernatural spirit of Arabian and Islamic folklore.

clue.text: Dog's odds initially double

blocks.note: SP, starting price, is the initial betting odds on a race
a ringer is a lookalike, as in a dead ringer

explanation.surface: A betting tip: the dog's opening odds are double.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is a racing abbreviation for starting price, the odds at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer is a spaniel breed used to flush, or spring, game birds for hunters.

clue.text: Speculator caught out in corporate manoeuvring

indicators.note: out means excluded, so that letter leaves the word it is in
manoeuvring means shifting things around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: A speculator is caught in boardroom intrigue and thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: An operator in finance is a dealer who trades shares on the market, hoping to profit from speculation.

clue.text: Show attitude after English vote

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first two in reading order

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a cross on a ballot paper marks a vote
a pose is a stance or affected attitude

explanation.surface: Someone shows their attitude once the English have voted.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose something is to reveal or display it, uncovering what was hidden from view.

clue.text: Marshal hoping to break strikes – the best bits?

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange or put in order, so the letters are reorganised
breaking into something means entering it, so these letters go inside another word

blocks.note: hits are blows or strikes
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A union official hopes industrial action will end, and asks for the highlights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikes' looks like industrial action, but it means blows; the question mark flags the definition's informal phrasing.
explanation.definitionFit: The high points of something are its peaks or most enjoyable moments, the highlights.

clue.text: Public cutting possible outcome of HMRC estimate?

blocks.note: overt means open, done in public view
axing is chopping or cutting

explanation.surface: Public spending cuts as a likely result of a tax authority's forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: HMRC is His Majesty's Revenue and Customs, the UK tax authority; an overestimate by it would charge too much.
explanation.definitionFit: If the taxman's estimate is too high, a person ends up charged excessive tax, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Fuel dumped in Calder Valley

indicators.note: something dumped in a place lies within it, so the letters sit inside the next words

blocks.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Fuel has been fly-tipped in a Yorkshire valley.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is the British name for diesel road fuel; Calder Valley is in West Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv is diesel oil for road vehicles, from diesel-engined road vehicle, so it is a type of fuel.

clue.text: Speed unit stopping still – on tail of Hillman Minx?

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so this unit fills the middle of another word
the tail of a word is its final letter
in an across clue, on means placed after the next piece

blocks.note: the final letter of the car maker's name
yet means still, as in not yet done
miles per hour is a unit of speed

explanation.surface: Talk of speed limits and a classic car, the Hillman Minx, standing still.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hillman Minx was a British family car; the definition is the last word alone, with the question mark admitting the shift in sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A minx is a flirtatious, provocative girl, close in sense to a sexually precocious young girl.

clue.text: Almost directly opposed horse entering curved track?

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the last letter is cut off
something entering goes inside, so this animal sits within the other word

blocks.note: polar opposites are directly opposed
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A horse veers onto a bending racecourse heading the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims only the first word, before the horse goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A projectile follows a parabolic path, so a parabola can be described as a curved track, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Unopened drinks players returned – genius!

indicators.note: something unopened is missing its start, so each word loses its first letter
returned means sent back, so the combined letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: port is a fortified wine
a team is a set of players

explanation.surface: A team returns to the bar for drinks still sealed and toasts a genius.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words lose their first letter: ORTS and EAM, then the whole is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master of an art, especially music, a great talent or virtuoso.

clue.text: Renounces a female visitor for undressing

indicators.note: undressing strips off the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: Irene is a woman's name
a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: A woman calls off a visitor's planned striptease.
explanation.walkthrough: IRENEGUEST loses its outer letters. RENEGUE is a variant spelling of renege.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise or abandon a commitment, giving it up.

clue.text: Briefly grumble about one former duchy

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped
about suggests moving around, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone briefly complains about a single old duchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Limburg was a medieval duchy straddling modern Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany.

clue.text: Extremely negative answer left for driver

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the first and last letters of each word

blocks.note: the first and last letters
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A firm no to a driver who asked to be let go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' applies to both words. The near side of a vehicle or horse is the left, in Britain the kerb side.
explanation.definitionFit: Near side is the traditional term for the left-hand side of a vehicle or a horse.

clue.text: Learn about collecting silver large $10 coins

indicators.note: about means turned round, so this word is read backwards
collecting means gathering in, so the other letters go inside

blocks.note: to see is to find out or learn
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A coin collector studies large silver pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle was a US gold coin worth ten dollars, named after its national bird emblem.

clue.text: Accumulating starch, say?

blocks.note: first meaning: building up or growing denser
second meaning: an ingredient added to make a sauce less runny

explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks starch as one example among several, such as flour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something growing dense, and as a noun names the agent cooks add to stiffen liquids.

clue.text: Pick up this marble for a quid

indicators.note: to pick up is to hear, so the answer is how a word is heard

blocks.note: nicker is British slang for a pound, a quid

explanation.surface: A child offered a marble for a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Quid and nicker are both British slang for one pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickar is the hard grey seed of a tropical shrub, used by children as a playing marble.

clue.text: One for carrying over broadcast

blocks.note: surface reading: a television or radio relay transmitter
setter's reading: over, when spoken, sounds like ova, meaning eggs

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a relay mast; read 'over' as spoken and you get ova, eggs, so this carries eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardboard egg box is a container designed for carrying eggs home without breaking them.

clue.text: Maybe Polly's home time changed after ditching HND

indicators.note: ditching means getting rid of, so those letters are thrown out of the word

blocks.note: bird is slang for time served in prison
taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Polly's home life changes after she drops her vocational diploma.
explanation.walkthrough: Doing bird is British slang for serving a jail sentence. Polly is a stock name for a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot such as Polly would typically live in a cage built for pet birds, hence maybe.

clue.text: A little cottage garden promoted in Vogue

indicators.note: a little means a small part, so the letters are a portion of the next words
promoted means raised, so in a down entry the letters read upwards

blocks.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A little cottage garden is featured in a fashion magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vogue' looks like the magazine but is the definition: something in vogue is the rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all the rage is in vogue, the height of fashion, so both nouns mean a craze.

clue.text: Half checks out ship's comfy chair

indicators.note: half means only part is kept, so the second three letters go

blocks.note: to recce is to reconnoitre, to check a place out
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: A passenger inspects the ship's armchairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Recce is British informal for reconnaissance.
explanation.definitionFit: A recliner is an armchair whose back tips backwards for lounging, a comfortable seat.

clue.text: Mallet for crushing river stones

indicators.note: crushing squeezes something tight, so the mallet word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: a gavel is a judge's or auctioneer's mallet
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Using a mallet to break up stones from a river bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravel is loose small stones or pebbles, used for paths and driveways.
